data.title: Will GameStop Stock (GME) Rise or Fall After Q2 Earnings?
data.description:
GameStop (GME) is set to report its Q2 2026 earnings after markets close on Tuesday. With that in mind, traders are wondering what they should expect from the video game retailer. That includes deeper insight into its stock movements, such as how the shares have moved after the company's recent earnings reports. If history is anything to go by, Q2 earnings could be a positive catalyst for GME stock.

Here's how GME stock has moved after the company's eight most recent earnings reports.

  • The trend flipped on March 26, 2024, with the stock dropping 15.03%.
  • The decline got much steeper on June 7, 2024, when shares tumbled 39.38% after earnings.
  • The selling continued on September 10, 2024, with the stock falling another 11.98%.
  • The trend turned positive on December 10, 2024, as shares gained 7.58% after the update.
  • Buying picked up on March 25, 2025, when the stock climbed 11.65%.
  • After a gap in the reporting data, shares were still moving higher on March 24, 2026, edging up 1.18%.
  • The period ended on June 2, 2026, with the stock adding another 6.02%.

GameStop stock has a good chance of rallying based on its historical movement, which saw shares rise in five of the past eight quarters.

data.title: Volkswagen Stock (VOW3) Rises on Plan to Cut 50,000 Jobs and Restructure Operations
data.description:
Shares of Volkswagen (DE:VOW3) closed up 7% on Sept. 4 after the German automaker announced plans to eliminate 50,000 jobs and restructure its operations. Volkswagen, Europe's largest automaker, announced the job cuts as part of its "Future Plan 2030" restructuring strategy. Management said the turnaround plan is the "most strategically profound transformation program" in the company's 89-year history.

The centerpiece of the transformation is 50,000 job cuts, including management positions. Volkswagen said the cuts are needed as it struggles with rising competition and tariff pressures. The latest workforce reduction is in addition to 50,000 job cuts that were previously announced, bringing the total staff rationalization at the company to 100,000 positions.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Tesla Stock's Cybercab Event Disappoints, and Shares Fall. This Analyst Sees Another 90% Drop
data.description:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares are falling in Friday's session, representing a reversal of Thursday's action. The stock gained more than 5% yesterday as investors looked ahead to the company's latest step toward autonomous ride-hailing. The excitement was centered on the Cybercab event and Elon Musk's ambition to challenge Waymo in the self-driving market.

By Friday, however, that enthusiasm had evaporated. TSLA shares are down 6.5% as of writing.

The company said Cybercab rides would open to the public in "limited areas" of Austin, Texas, at 5 p.m. CT on Friday. But the highly anticipated launch event itself was remarkably low-key. There was no livestream, journalists were excluded, and Elon Musk did not attend. Instead, Tesla invited a small group of largely pro-Tesla content creators, who were given rides in the two-seat vehicle.

Promotion

Explore TSLQ for 2X short leverage on TSLA

The company also provided few details about the commercial rollout. It did not disclose pricing or a specific deployment target, while Tesla's app reportedly did not allow users to request a Cybercab ride as of Thursday night. There are 45 Cybercabs registered in Texas.

Adding to the disappointment, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into the Cybercab's self-certification under federal vehicle safety standards, focusing on the vehicle's lack of a steering wheel and conventional pedals. Questions also remain over potential resistance from states to Tesla's camera-only approach to autonomous driving.

For GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson, the muted event was hardly surprising. "We've learned to keep a simple rule for Tesla product launches: count what can be counted. Last night we could count one thing, and that was 45 Cybercab registrations with the Texas DMV as of Wednesday," Johnson said.

The analyst argues that Tesla failed to provide several of the metrics investors were looking for, including deployment targets, pricing and a consumer ordering option. "Attendees, a curated group of Tesla-friendly creators/cultists with instructions that plus-ones could not themselves be creators, took rides in a two-seater with no steering wheel and no pedals. Then they posted about it. That was the event," he scathingly added.

Johnson does acknowledge that Tesla has made meaningful engineering progress, with the Cybercab going from little more than a stage prop in Burbank 23 months ago to carrying passengers on public roads today. "But the stock is not priced for a car," he went on to say. "It is priced for a network, and on the network the company told us nothing it had not already said."

Johnson also took aim at Wall Street's expectations. Morgan Stanley had written ahead of the event that 25 to 50 Cybercabs operating across Texas could potentially lift Tesla shares, while the bullish scenario involved paid, unsupervised rides in Austin, Houston and Dallas.

Instead, Tesla delivered a much narrower rollout in Austin, with no clear indication of how many of the 45 registered vehicles are actually operating. "Sell-the-news" is Johnson's conclusion, something investors apparently took to heart.

However, Johnson evidently thinks the stock is still completely overvalued. Along with a Sell rating, his $24.86 price target suggests the stock will fall another 93% over the next year. (To watch Johnson's track record, click here)

Two other analysts are also TSLA bears, yet with an additional 11 Buys and 14 Holds, the stock claims a Moderate Buy consensus rating. At $377.08, the average price target suggests the stock will gain 7% in the months ahead. (See Tesla stock forecast)

data.title: PayPal Stock (PYPL) Falls as Company Pauses $1 Billion Venture Portfolio Sale
data.description:
Payments company PayPal (PYPL) has reportedly paused plans to sell its venture capital portfolio after potential buyers offered much less than the company hoped to receive. According to Axios Pro, PayPal had been exploring a sale of roughly $900 million to $1 billion in investments. However, the highest offers came in at around 60 cents on the dollar, which may have convinced PayPal that now is not the best time to sell. As a result, shares are down in today's trading.

The decision comes as fintech valuations remain relatively weak. Therefore, selling the portfolio today could force PayPal to accept a large discount compared with what those investments might be worth if valuations recover. PayPal began exploring a sale earlier this year after deciding to wind down its corporate venture capital arm in order to increase its focus on core operations. The company hired investment bank Jefferies (JEF) to advise on the process.

The portfolio includes investments in companies such as shopping app Tabby and crypto platform Anchorage. Nevertheless, pausing the sale does not necessarily mean that strategy has changed. Instead, PayPal may simply be waiting for a better opportunity to sell.

On the other hand, keeping the portfolio means PayPal will continue to hold investments that it previously decided were no longer central to its strategy.

The news comes during another volatile week for PayPal shares. Today's stock decline erased much of Thursday's roughly 4% gain. That earlier rally came after talks of a potential takeover of the company restarted.

PayPal is also going through a restructuring. Indeed, it was reported this week that the company is cutting about 220 jobs in India as part of a multi-year plan to improve efficiency.

data.title: Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Slips With Launch of Project Zenith
data.description:
Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) recently brought out its new Project Zenith, which has been described as a "distraction-free Windows experience for developers." That could be a pretty big step forward, and could give Microsoft a significant advantage when it comes to supplying the shovels in the gold rush of Windows development. Investors did not seem convinced, though, and Microsoft shares slipped nearly 2% in Friday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 3.05% rally in its share price over the past year.

A Big Win for Devs

Project Zenith got something like a mention back at the Build show earlier this year, noted a report from The Verge. Now, Project Zenith has a lot more skin on its bones, and plenty of muscle as well. Project Zenith devices come with a "…preconfigured Windows setup for development and a set of tools curated for what developers reach for first," according to Windows platform and developer corporate vice president Logan Iyer.

Tools that come standard on every Project Zenith device include PowerToys, GitHub Copilot, Visual Studio Code, and more. Start menu tips start turned off, as are account notifications. The PowerToys Command Palette, meanwhile, starts enabled from the word go.

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Stumbles as Upbeat Jobs Data Sends Rate Hike Odds Higher
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.5% on Friday after stronger-than-expected labor market data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) sent rate hike expectations higher. The BLS said this morning that nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August, nearly tripling the consensus economist estimate of 55,000. In addition, the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%.

A healthy jobs market reduces the Fed's need to cut rates to support employment. That gives policymakers more room to focus on inflation instead. Inflation has remained above the central bank's 2% target for 65 consecutive months. Following the jobs report, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting jumped to 60.4% from 49.4% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

That didn't sit well with President Trump, who threatened to end trade with countries which the U.S. has a deficit with unless the Fed cuts rates. He added that "strong" countries should have lower rates and expressed disappointment with stocks falling in reaction to the jobs report. "The Fed Board, with its great new leader, must get smart – BE PATRIOTS for a change," Trump said in a Truth Social post.

data.title: Trump Threatens to End Trade With Deficit Countries Unless Fed Slashes Rates
data.description:
President Trump threatened on Friday to eliminate trade with countries which the U.S. carries a deficit unless the Fed lowers interest rates. The U.S. currently has a trade deficit with several key trading partners, including China, Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Germany.

"LOWER THE RATE OR I'LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT," Trump said in a Truth Social post. "IT'S BETTER THAN TARIFFS!" he added.

Strong Payrolls Lift Fed Rate Hike Expectations

Trump's statement came after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced that nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, well above expectations of 55,000. In addition, the unemployment rate remained unchanged from the prior month at 4.1%. However, rate hike expectations rose following the data, as a stronger labor market gives the Fed flexibility to raise rates. That comes as inflation has remained above the central bank's 2% target for 65 consecutive months.

data.title: Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Plunges, a Look at the Day After the Debut
data.description:
So yesterday was the big day for electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA), as it formally debuted the Cybercab. This was supposed to be a big day for Tesla, and normally, Tesla understands the value of a good show. Oddly, though, this debut proved a lot more quiet than many expected, and that may have hurt the value that the show generated. Investors agreed, and showed their discontent, sending Tesla shares down over 6% in Friday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 5.46% rally in its share price over the past year.

The Oddly Subdued Reveal of The Next Big Thing

A Tesla event, noted a report from Wired, is usually a big thing. Electronic music starts the affair, Elon Musk himself shows up, products are demonstrated, huge claims are made that occasionally need to be walked back later, and even "one more thing" shows up. But this time, there was a lot missing. Musk did not show up to the event. There was no livestream, and so-called Tesla influencers were forbidden from talking about the event until well after it had actually started.

Competitors Lose Staff

Meanwhile, Tesla's competition in the large electric truck space just got a lot slimmer. Windrose, one of the main competitors Tesla had in EV trucks, lost most of its Chinese staff, around 100 workers total. A Wall Street Journal report suggested that those departing were owed back pay. The report noted that Windrose has made partial payments, but when any part of workers' salaries is in arrears, you know the conditions on the ground are terrible. Just to round things out, the report noted that Windrose is also facing a lawsuit and regulators are increasingly taking notice.

data.title: Netflix Stock (NFLX) Falls 4% as Streamer Raises Price in the U.K.
data.description:
Netflix (NFLX) stock is down 4% on Sept. 4 after the company raised prices for its streaming service in the United Kingdom. The company has lifted the price of its its Standards with Ads streaming plan by a hefty 33% to GBP 7.99 (US$10.80) per month from GBP 5.99 previously. Additionally, Netflix increase its Standard streaming plan without advertisements 7.7% to GBP 13.99 per month from GBP 12.99. And the company hike its Premium ad-free streaming tier 10.5% to GBP 20.99 a month from GBP 18.99.

The new prices in the United Kingdom are effective immediately, according to Netflix, which has more than18 million subscribers in the U.K. Analysts and investors can grow nervous when streaming companies such as Netflix raise prices as it can lead to a wave of cancelations that leads to few subscribers and less revenue over the long run.

NFLX Stock Struggles

Netflix last raised its prices in the U.S. in March of this year, increasing the ad-supported tier by $1 to $8.99 a month and its ad-free tiers by $2 per month. The increased prices have not seemed to help Netflix or its financial results. In July, the company announced a mixed quarterly print that sent its share price down 10% in a single trading session.
